newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to get Romanian rail cars to ship grains.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to get Romanian rail cars to ship grains.

text.p: Hungary's national rail company MAV Rt will borrow 500 rail carriages from Romanian railways (SNCFR) to cope with grains exports expected to reach 800,000 tonnes this year, MAV said on Tuesday.
"We based our preparations on agriculture ministry forecasts for grains exports," Istvan Siklosi of MAV's logistics department told Reuters.
He added that MAV has reached another agreement with SNCFR to hire some 1,000 open-platform, four-axle rail cars for domestic sugar beet transport.
Both agreements are effective from August 1 and run until the end of the year, Siklosi said.
The move comes after traders said earlier that the agriculture ministry's October 31 deadline for grains export licences could cause some problems due to insufficient rail transport capacity.
Siklosi said he expected about half of Hungary's grains exports to go by rail.
Last year MAV exported some 300,000 tonnes of grain, compared with 2.5 million tonnes in 1995.
Another MAV official said the company has some 250 to 350 wagons suitable for grain transport and over the last years MAV has usually used Romanian rolling stock to handle high grains volumes.
Ministry and industry sources expect an 1997 wheat crop of around five million tonnes, up from last year's 3.9 million, leaving at least 1.5 million tonnes for export.
Although other east European countries such as Ukraine and Romania also expected good wheat crops, traders said Hungary's export hopes were recently boosted by the Czech and Polish floods.

Hungary's Agriculture Ministry announced in June that it will put only a time limit on grain exports this year, rather than a volume ceiling as in previous years, by issuing unlimited export licenses valid until October 31. --Denes Albert, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
